items.title: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
items.original_title: Generational gains in cognitive capacity and dementia incidence rates in Western countries
items.summary: The risk of developing dementia at any given age has fallen steadily in Europe and the United States over recent decades. A key unresolved question is whether recent generations reach older age with better cognitive capacity, experience slower cognitive decline, or both, as this has implications for when preventive interventions are likely to have the greatest impact. Analyzing ~783,000 episodic-memory assessments from ~219,000 individuals in five longitudinal studies followed for up to 30 years, we find that later-born generations benefit from a double dividend, with higher memory levels entering old age and slower decline thereafter. The combined advantage is large enough to plausibly account for the reported 13% per-decade decline in dementia incidence. Improvements are concentrated among the fastest decliners;

recommendation_reasons.research: 该研究基于约21.9万人的长期纵向队列和约78.3万次记忆评估，把世代认知优势拆成“进入老年时水平更高”和“下降更慢”两部分，并对应临床损害与海马萎缩，为痴呆发病率下降提供了机制层面的证据。限制在于这是观察性队列，不能证明因果，也不能据此评估具体预防干预的效应。

items.title: Medical Imaging and Pediatric and Adolescent Brain Tumor Risk.
items.original_title: Medical Imaging and Pediatric and Adolescent Brain Tumor Risk.
items.summary: Importance Ionizing radiation from medical imaging may increase brain tumor risk. Objective To quantify brain tumor risk associated with radiation exposure from medical imaging in children and adolescents. Design, setting, and participants Retrospective cohort study of children born from 1996 through 2016 who were enrolled from birth in 6 US health care systems or Ontario, Canada, and were alive and cancer-free at age 2 years, with follow-up through December 31, 2017 (US sites), and December 31, 2024 (Ontario). Exposures Cumulative radiation dose to the brain from medical imaging, lagged by 2 years. Main outcomes and measures Incident brain or other central nervous system tumors. Hazard ratios (HRs) were estimated using Cox proportional hazards models for categorical dose, and excess relative risks (ERRs) were estimated using linear dose-response models for continuous dose.

items.title: Medicare Shared Savings Program Accountable Care Organizations Performance Year 2025 Financial and Quality Results
items.original_title: Medicare Shared Savings Program Accountable Care Organizations Performance Year 2025 Financial and Quality Results
items.summary: Medicare Shared Savings Program Accountable Care Organizations Performance Year 2025 Financial and Quality Results Medicare Shared Savings Program (Shared Savings Program) Accountable Care Organizations (ACOs) are critical in helping Make America Healthy Again — by supporting high-quality, coordinated care that addresses prevention, chronic illness and the root causes of disease. For Performance Year (PY) 2025, ACOs in the Shared Savings Program achieved the highest rates of shared savings since the inception of the program. ACOs that achieved savings had lower utilization compared to their benchmark across many categories of utilization including hospital discharges, Emergency Department (ED) Visits, number of Skilled Nursing Facility (SNF) stays, and SNF Utilization Days.

recommendation_reasons.industry: 这是Medicare共享节余计划PY2025的官方结算与质量结果，并披露CY2027支付规则对ACO激励、基准调整、数字质量报告和Part B自付减免的最终政策；产业读者可据此判断责任医疗组织的付费阶段、风险轨道迁移和参与策略，但材料为CMS汇总口径，缺少ACO层面明细和因果设计。

items.title: Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.original_title: Once-Weekly Ribupatide for Weight Loss in Adults in China With Overweight or Obesity: The GEMINI-1 Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: Importance Obesity is a major health problem in China; more pharmacotherapy choices for long-term weight management are needed. Objective To evaluate the efficacy and safety of once-weekly subcutaneous ribupatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide/glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, for weight loss in adults in China with overweight or obesity without diabetes. Design, setting, and participants This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 clinical trial was conducted at 55 sites in China. From May to June 2024, adults without diabetes who had a body mass index of 28 or greater or 24 or greater with at least 1 weight-related comorbidity were enrolled, with final follow-up on June 20, 2025.

items.title: Tirzepatide in Adolescents With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.original_title: Tirzepatide in Adolescents With Obesity: The SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS Randomized Clinical Trial.
items.summary: Importance Information on the effects of tirzepatide, a once-weekly glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist approved for obesity management in adults with obesity, remains limited in adolescents. Overall, 79.6% of tirzepatide-treated participants achieved BMI reduction of at least 5% compared with 28.5% of participants in the placebo group (risk difference, 51.2 [95% CI, 36.3-66.1] percentage points; P < .001).

items.title: Expansion and cytotoxicity of mucosal CAR<sup>+</sup> T cells in enterocolitis associated with BCMA CAR-T cell therapy
items.original_title: Expansion and cytotoxicity of mucosal CAR<sup>+</sup> T cells in enterocolitis associated with BCMA CAR-T cell therapy
items.summary: Ciltacabtagene autoleucel (cilta-cel) is a B cell maturation-antigen-targeting chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell product approved for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma treatment. Previously reported cases of post-cilta-cel immune effector cell enterocolitis (IEC-EC) have been described as a severe diarrhea associated with clonal CAR T cell populations. Here we report nine cases of cilta-cel-associated IEC-EC with CAR T cell-positive (CAR+) infiltration in 158 cilta-cel-treated patients at MD Anderson Cancer Center (incidence of 5.1% at a 6-month landmark and 5.7% globally). Cilta-cel infiltration was the primary cause of IEC-EC, and all cases demonstrated monoclonal or oligoclonal T cell populations as measured by vector integration analysis, flow cytometry and T cell receptor sequencing.

items.title: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
items.original_title: Seasonal mass vaccination with R21/Matrix-M against malaria in The Gambia and Burkina Faso: an open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial.
items.summary: Background The R21/Matrix-M (R21) malaria vaccine candidate, recommended by WHO for use in young children, could be extended to the whole population. Seasonal mass vaccination (SMV) before peak malaria transmission could be a promising tool to accelerate progress towards malaria elimination. We aimed to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of SMV with R21 in two malaria-endemic settings in west Africa. Methods This open-label, cluster-randomised, controlled trial was conducted in The Gambia, a setting with low-to-moderate seasonal transmission, and Burkina Faso, a setting with intense seasonal transmission. 54 medium-sized villages (30 in The Gambia and 24 in Burkina Faso) were randomly assigned (1:1) by use of computer-restricted randomisation to receive either SMV with R21 (intervention group) or no SMV (control group).

items.title: Artificial intelligence model for pancreatic cancer risk prediction in patients with pancreatic cystic lesions
items.original_title: Artificial intelligence model for pancreatic cancer risk prediction in patients with pancreatic cystic lesions
items.summary: Cancer risk assessment is a crucial step in PCL management, but the complexity and limited accuracy of existing approaches contribute to suboptimal patient care. We developed and validated an artificial intelligence (AI) model that uses radiology reports and clinical data to predict the future risk of pancreatic cancer in patients with PCLs. Among the models evaluated, XGBoost achieved the highest performance, with AUCs of 0.960, 0.945, and 0.944 for predicting pancreatic cancer incidence at 1, 3, and 5 years after imaging, respectively.
